items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: And then there was Chu Berry who also had a different

ctx.x: Or his confusion that you speak of. And I felt very close to Ben Webster. I believe he was born on the same astrological sign as I, Aries. And I admired his work, and the fact of the matter is if you want to speak in terms of competition, there was quite some controversy for the many early years of jazz that Ben Webster perhaps was classed as one of the top three or four tenor saxophone players in those days when there was Coleman Hawkins considered to be the father, the grandfather, and the originator of the…
And then there was Chu Berry who also had a different

musical approach. And Ben Webster had his own qualities, which was classified along with these great tenor saxophone players, you know. But as I said, I think that his struggle, and it's the same -- I think every artist in any field has this and I think they have to deal with this. And it comes apart in your life, and I've had my share of it and I'm having my share of it now. And you asked me did I struggle. Yes, I'm still struggling because it starts with your ability to improve yourself. And this comes in…
